utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone in this courtroom at the beginning of this week. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. We were informed last week that Mr. Piletta-Zanin will not be present today, so you're just on your own, Ms. Pilipovic. Is there anything at the beginning of the week? Sometimes parties have thought of things during the weekend, but you all seem to be rather quiet, so nothing specific. Then I think it's up to you, Ms. Pilipovic, to continue your cross-examination of the witness, Ms. Omerovic. Please, Mr. Usher, could you bring in the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As I indicated to you last Friday, the cross-examination by Ms. Pilipovic will now continue. Ms. Pilipovic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Good afternoon to everyone. Cross-examined by Ms. Pilipovic: [Continued].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Ms. Omerovic.

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On Friday, when we started our questions, I believe that we stopped at the moment when you told us that at the time when you gave the statement to the investigators of the Tribunal in 1995, it was on the 8th of November, you said that your memory was fresher at that time. Do you remember that? Do you remember that answer that you gave?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the examination-in-chief by my learned colleague, you told us about the incident that happened on the 26th of June, 1994. Could you tell us what time that was?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Between 1900 and 1930.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us, considering that this was the month of June, what was the visibility and what kind of day that was.

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a sunny day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that you had set off to see your sister. Could you tell us what part of town does your sister live in?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was returning from my sister's.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you tell us that you were going to get a book?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us in which part of town does your sister live?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the same locality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us what is the name of the locality?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vojnicko Polje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before the incident that happened, what is the time that elapsed, that you went to your sister's until the incident?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About two hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On your way to your sister's, did you take the same route?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Until the -- is there another route that you could take to your sister's apartment?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you had taken this other route, would you have avoided the danger of being exposed to some armed attack, considering you said you were on or near the line of confrontation?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The question was is there another route that you could have taken to your sister's apartment. The witness's evidence is that the incident took place on the way from her sister's apartment. Thank you, Mr. President. The relevance of my objection becomes clear in the next question, at page 3, line 11.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Pilipovic, as far as I understand, Mr. Ierace thinks that taking different routes the way to the sister is not relevant since the incident happened on the way back from her sister's. Would you please either indicate what the relevance is or rephrase your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I will rephrase my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the way to your sister's that day, considering that you were on your way back when the incident occurred, could you tell us what is the route that you took?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same route.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On your way back from your sister's, you said that you were going to get a book. Could you tell us, how far was the front line away from the place where you and your friend found yourselves the moment that you said that you saw that her top -- her shirt was bloody, covered in blood?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us -- that was page 69, line 14. The question asked by my learned colleague, you said that the soldiers ran up to us and took her to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us where the soldiers were?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the other side of the street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "on the other side of the street," could you say that in a more accurate way? Could you tell us exactly where in front of a building, inside a building, next to a building, on the pavement? Where exactly were the soldiers that ran up to you?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The soldiers were in the building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say that they were in the building, how many were there?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Four or five.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say they were in the building, could you tell us more accurately, what do you mean by "in the building"? Were they at the door, the window, in front of the building? By considering you said "in the building," could you tell us what exactly you mean by "in the building"?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were at the window.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does the building have floors?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which floor?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the second and the third floor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us: These soldiers, what were they wearing? How did you know they were soldiers?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had uniforms on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see if they were armed?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When they approached you, or rather, your friend, how many approached her?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Three of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you then see that they had weapons?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see them before they approached you?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see these soldiers when you were going to your sister's?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you say that the very first moment that you saw these soldiers that were on the second and third floor of that building, in front of which the incident occurred, you said that before that you didn't see them.

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. I've made a mistake. I saw them before that, when they warned us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When they warned you, when was that?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was prior to the incident.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us what did that warning consist of?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They said -- they told us to hurry up because a few moments before sniper fire had been opened and some people had been passing by.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you and your friend hear the fire, the firing?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did. We heard one shot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long before did that happen before your friend told you that she was injured?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The shot happened when she was injured.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As far as I remember, you said that the soldiers had warned you that fire had been opened.

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear any other fire before that shot, about the fire that the soldiers had warned you about?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that you hid in a trench, you took cover in a trench, you and your friend.

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us if in that trench there were soldiers?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How often, in relation to the incident that occurred -- and I'm going to be precise -- in 1994, how frequently did you pass that portion of that route? When I say "frequently," what I mean is, for instance, weekly. How often did you go there?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Three or four times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In 1994, since you went frequently, three or four times a week, did you see soldiers in that portion of the route?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the course of 1994, did you see or hear shooting towards Nedzarici and from Nedzarici towards the positions where you saw the soldiers?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us whether in the vicinity of the building where you lived and the building where your sister lived and the building where the incident happened, were there military facilities near these buildings?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us: These soldiers who were on the second and the third floor, do you know who these soldiers were?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where they spent the night?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the conflict, which lasted in this area in 1992, 1993, and 1994, do you have any knowledge whether the citizens, specifically in the building where you lived or in other buildings, whether citizens were organised in a sense that they protected their buildings and guarded the entrances to the buildings?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever, in the part of the building where you lived or in your sister's building, did you see soldiers in 1992, 1993, and 1994?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in 1992 and 1993, but yes, in 1994.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said, asked by my learned colleague, that in the period after the conflict started, you did not leave your building. You said that you were with your family in the cellar of that building. Could you tell us what was the period?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From 1992 to 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go to school?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether other children from the building that you lived in, and other buildings, did they go to school?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I tell you that you told us that your memory when you gave the statement in 1995, that your memory was fresher, how could you explain that then in your statement you didn't tell us that in the period between 1992 and 1993 you spent in the cellar of your building?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I object, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We never talked about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The question is unfair. It presumes that she should have included such an aspect in her statement, and there's no reason to presume that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can read the statement of the -- the witness statement. It's very short, and I read it very carefully. And the witness never told us in her statement in 1992 and 1993 that she was in the trench, and I have the statement both in B/C/S and in English. And my question is because she said that her memory was fresher when she gave the statement, so I'm wondering why she never spoke about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's not the issue. The issue is whether she did not say anything about it where she could have expected to have done so or whether it was just not asked of her. And, of course, we cannot expect from someone just to come up with all things he or she thinks to be relevant, questions, but let me just confirm with my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The objection is sustained. The reasons given by Mr. Ierace are valid. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, when the incident happened that you told us about, can you tell us where your friend went to hospital? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. To Dobrinja.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us if these soldiers who were near you, or you Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. yourself, did you report this incident to some of the authorities, to the authorities?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us if in the vicinity of the buildings where you were, that is, where you lived, and on your way to your sister's, did you see whether in that area there was an observation post of the UN?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether any of the soldiers who had approached you to help, whether they reported to the UN soldiers that an incident occurred?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On Friday, you told us that in the spring of 1994 you heard, while you were by a window in your apartment, that a young boy, Dejan Stevanovic, was killed.

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, in relation to the incident which occurred while you were with your sister, could you tell us when did this other incident occur? Presumably it was -- when did that other incident happen?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: -- The question again misstates the evidence. The question presumes that the shooting incident happened when this witness was with her sister. She was coming from her sister's place and was with a friend. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, I do understand that this is the second incident, not the incident where you returned from your sister's, so let me just check what else has been said on the presence of your sister at that moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, Your Honour. I did not ask that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What I see at this moment is that -- yes, it doesn't say.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can repeat the question, but my question certainly was not this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, I do not see in the transcript anything -- that there was anything about being with her sister, or I'm -- one moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're saying that the question was about being with her sister at that moment. 14. Let me just see. 14. Yes, I think it's a matter of misunderstanding, Mr. Ierace. The question was: "Can you tell us, in relation to the incident that occurred while you were with your sister, can you tell us when did this other incident occur?" So that other incident was the incident, not the one when she was with or going to or returning from her sister. That's how I understood it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And if that's the case, Mr. President, then that does reflect the evidence. The words used by my friend were to the effect that this witness was with her sister when the friend was shot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. She was not, but I think the questioning was now about the other incident, so -- yes, please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So I'm going to repeat my question. So you were present when the ten-year-old boy, Dejan Stevanovic, was killed. As far as I can remember, you said that you were by the window, that you were looking at it.

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question is: In relation to the incident on the 26th of June, when you were with your friend -- that was in the summer -- can you tell us in terms of a time frame when was this other incident when Dejan Stevanovic was killed?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the moment when you were looking at that incident, what did you see from your window, if you were looking from your window?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went to the window when I heard a noise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "went to the window," can you please tell us what you mean.

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I looked through the window. I saw a boy who was lying on the ground. There were many people surrounding him, including my brother. After that, his father ran out and he saw that he was dead.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you speak to the parents of the boy who was killed?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they tell you whether they knew where Dejan had been shot from?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They could only presume, but they did not know exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were at the window, did you hear a shot or was there shooting during that day? Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Today you told us that you were at the window.

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I went to the window after I heard the noise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you allow for the possibility that you were on the balcony? Does your building have a balcony?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you allow for the possibility that you could have been on the balcony?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us: On that day, what was the weather like?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether the parents of Dejan Stevanovic reported this incident to the police?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the time of day?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you said that people gathered there, did you see if there were any UN monitors there?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, with your leave, the Defence would like to show photograph 3279OO, P3279OO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Pilipovic. These are two photographs. Could you please indicate whether you would like to have number 08 or 17A on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. 08.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you have before you a photograph, the same photograph that was shown you on Friday. Can you tell us if the building that you can see in the forefront, or rather, the part of the building that you can see on this photograph, can you explain to us if this part of the building existed already before the conflict or is it a building under construction, as my learned friend suggested? Can you be more precise and tell us if this is part of a demolished building or a building under construction?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a part of a demolished -- of a destroyed building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us: This part of the building that you tell us was destroyed, when was that? Do you know when that happened?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the war started, from 1992 onwards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us: How tall was this building, how many floors it had?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was an eighth-storey building, that is, the ground floor and seven floors.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us if it was a building where civilians lived or was it an office building?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a civilian building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us on which side of the line of conflict was this building? When I say "the side of the line of the conflict," I mean, to be precise, whether on the side of the line of the conflict controlled by the BH army or on the side of the line of conflict under the control of the army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the side controlled by the BH army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you agree with me when I put it to you that in that part of the building, in that part of the locality, there was fighting, since you said that the building had eight floors and that they were all destroyed?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I shall be more precise. Can you tell us whether this building was destroyed because of the fighting?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The building was shelled.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us when was that? I shall be precise. In 1992, in 1993, or 1994?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From 1992 onwards, it was constantly under shell fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge if in that part of the building, the ground floor of the building, the troops of the BH army were quartered?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On this photograph behind this building, we can see other buildings, including a building, and that is the orange building with white stripes, that you tell us that that is where the incident happened. Can you show us on this photograph the building where you lived?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. [indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To be precise, for the record, can you tell us: Can one see this building behind the tree or is it -- or can we only see the roof of the building, the white roof?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One can see the building.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, with your leave, I'd like to ask the witness to take the black marker and circle the building so that everybody can be clear about this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please, would you put a circle around the building where you were living at that time.

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I understand you right, but I stand to be corrected if I didn't, your windows did not face this side that we can see here; it faced the other side. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. In this part of the buildings that we can see, can one also see your sister's building, whom you visited that day?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you can.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you then circle that building too so that we can see the route that you took.

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For the record, would you please put number 1 in this first circle, and then number 1 the building where the witness lived and the number 2, and put a small 2 in that small circle. Yes, for the record, number 1 is the building where the witness lived, number 2 is the building where the witness's sister lived. Witness, can you tell us: This building that you lived in on the ground floor of this building facing the side that was damaged, do you know if on the ground floor of that building there were present the soldiers of the BH army?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge if -- I shall be precise -- 1992 -- 1993, excuse me, 1993 and 1994, whether, in relation to this part of the building where you lived, were there any armed operations? Was there any fighting in that part of the city between the two armies?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us if any member of your family was a member of the BH army?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. My father, in 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge gained from your father, who was a member of the BH army, if he took part in the fighting?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you -- since you told us that in 1992 and 1993 you didn't attend school, did you attend school in 1994?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us: Where is it that you attended school? In what part of the city was your school?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On this photograph, where we see those buildings, can you point at the school building, if one can see it, or is it that you cannot see it?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You cannot see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you -- to go to school, did you use the same route that you used to go to your sister's?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you went to school, or on your way back, did you, during those intervals in that part of the area that you lived in, could you hear any gunfire?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I could.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you determine from which part of the city this gunfire was coming from?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us which part of the city is it?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nedzarici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you see that or is it that you only could hear it?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge -- did you, after 1994, or in 1995, did you ever go to Nedzarici?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us if in that part of the city there were any damage to structures, like your building over there?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence has finished its cross-examination. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Ms. Pilipovic. Mr. Ierace, are you in any need of re-examination of the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I won't be long, I don't think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed. Re-examined by Mr. Ierace:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have to your right the photograph about which you were asked Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. questions by my learned colleague. She asked you about a building in the photograph that you said was partly demolished, and you said that it had eight storeys. Could you please take the pointer and point to the remains of that building in the photograph? Do you remember that you were asked those questions?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I think you said that it had been shelled from 1992 onwards. It was constantly under shell fire. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Could you please point to that building.

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you indicate the building complex in which you lived, which you circled, and has a number 1 on it?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, just a few moments ago you were asked by my learned colleague if you had been to Nedzarici, and you said that you had. When was that? When did you first go there after the conflict or during the conflict?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1998, 1999, thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go to the School for the Blind?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you walk through the buildings?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see in those buildings that you walked through any signs consistent with the buildings having been used for small arms fire?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any holes in the walls?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Nothing further, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. I am wondering, Ms. Pilipovic, before I give the opportunity to my colleagues to ask any additional questions, when you asked questions about a building of which the witness later said that it was constantly being shelled, you were talking about the building in the forefront. Was that -- in your questioning, did you aim at the building which was circled and given number 1 or were you questioning the witness about the just ground floor structure in front of the photograph?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my first question concerning the photograph and the building on the photograph, which you can see, my question had to do with this part of the building, because I wanted the witness to explain to us the front one, the white part, whether this was a building under construction or whether there used to be a building beforehand, and the witness said that this was a building which had the ground floor and seven floors, that is, an eight-storey building and that that building had been destroyed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I -- one moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you would just give me one second, please. I'd just like to be completely sure about approximate that there's no misunderstanding as far as the buildings is concerned. Mr. Usher, could you please put back on the ELMO again photo 3279OO, and the first photograph, 08. Ms. Omerovic, questions have been put to you in relation to buildings. You told, upon a question of Ms. Pilipovic, about a building of which -- which used to have seven or eight storeys. Is that the building just in front of the photograph, that is to say, the building with the -- I would say the two or three dark holes down in the building, or were you --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would have no objection to the usher using the pointer and pointing to that building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Usher, could you please assist me. Yes, if you're doing it yourself. There's a one-storey structure in the left of the photograph. Could you please point at it so that we can see it with the pointer, please. Could you please use the pointer. Yes, that one. Was that a seven or eight-storey high building before?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So when you told us about a seven- or eight-storey-high building, were you then answering the question in relation to the building you made a circle around with number 1 on the right-hand side? Please point at it so that we are sure that ...

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's the building with the seven or eight storeys you told us about; is that true?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And in the forefront of the photograph, the -- could you please point at it again, the white one --

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Below there. Yes. Has that ever been a high-rise building or has it always been low?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the same building. This is a shopping centre.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And it never was six, seven, or eight storeys high; it always was as low as you see it on the photograph?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, I was asking this because I was thinking of whatever misunderstanding by the witness as far as your questions were concerned. Let me just look at the transcript at this moment. It says, on page 14, line 13 -- you asked how many floors the building had, and as far as I was aware of, you were asking about this low-storey -- this low building, and only later turned to the apartment blocks on the right-hand side of the photograph. So since it seems that the witness might have misunderstood your question in this respect, if you'd like to ask any additional questions, although part of what you would like to know has been answered already, while I tried to find out whether there was any misunderstanding. But I think it's fair that if your question has been misunderstood, that if there are any additional questions, you may put them to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Thank you, Your Honour. Further cross-examination by Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, can you tell us about this building which you identified a moment ago and said that it was a shopping centre? Can you tell us if -- on which line of the conflict was this building in 1992, 1993, and 1994? Do you have any knowledge about that?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in between.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "in between," does it mean that it was on the front line itself?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was that the situation throughout the conflict or did this line shift?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did this building look like this before the conflict broke out or it changed its appearance in 1992, 1993, and 1994?

utterances.speaker: MEDINA OMEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It changed its appearance.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Pilipovic. Mr. Ierace, if at this point there would be any need to re-examine the witness, then of course you will have it. Thank you. Have any of my colleagues have any additional questions? Ms. Omerovic, you have been answering a lot of questions, both on Friday and today. As you'll understand, it's very important for this Court to establish the truth, to get the information from those who have been present at that time, at those places, and while answering the questions of the Prosecution and the Defence and the questions additionally put to you by the Bench, I think you have given -- you have assisted this Court in performing its task, and its task is taking decisions on the matters that are before this Court. I'd like to thank you very much for coming a very, very long way from Sarajevo to The Hague and assisting the Court by answering all these questions from all the parties and the Bench. I also wish you a safe trip home again, and thank you very much for coming. Mr. Usher, would you please lead Ms. Omerovic out of the courtroom after it has been translated what I said to her.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, I think we have some documents on which we have to decide whether they are admitted into evidence. I think the first one is P320 -- 80O, which is the video, if I'm correct. Is that correct? Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I'm trying to assist you, since you're not here all the time. The second one are two photographs, and I think they are P3279OO.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, bearing the ERN numbers 0106-1210/08 and 0106-1219/17A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Then we have, I think, two more photographs, under P3270.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes. Bearing the ERN numbers 02114226 and 02114227.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think then next we have the 360-degree photograph on CD-ROM, which would be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the last one is a map that was premarked by the witness by giving an earlier statement, and that would be?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So apart from the -- I would say the standing objections against the 360-degree photographs, no further objection, they're admitted into evidence. Mr. Ierace, am I right in my understanding that your next witness to be called will be Fuad Dziho?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Usher, would you please lead the witness into the courtroom. [The witness entered court].

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, before that witness is called, was there not also a Defence Exhibit in relation to the last witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Wasn't this -- I think there was some marking made on the -- or am I wrong?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I stand corrected, Mr. President. I think the marking was on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It was on a Prosecution Exhibit. It was marked with black, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Which was I think P3279OO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I asked specifically to put either the 08 or the 17A photograph to the witness. I apologise for -- please, would you ... I apologise that you had to wait for some final things we had to deal with. Do you understand me -- do you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're Mr. Dziho?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before giving testimony in this court, Mr. Dziho, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. The text of that declaration will be given to you by the usher, and I invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Witness answered through interpreter].

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please be seated. What I should have said when we were still dealing with other matters is welcome into this courtroom, Mr. Dziho. You have been called as a witness by the Prosecution --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You will first be examined by the counsel for the Prosecution and then later on you will be examined by counsel for the Defence. Mr. Ierace, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Examined by Mr. Ierace:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, would you please give your full name for the purposes of the record.

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: My name is Fuad Dziho.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In 1992, whereabouts were you living?

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: I was living in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I should indicate, Mr. President, that this evidence concerns scheduled sniping incident number 21.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was your occupation at the -- immediately before the commencement of the armed conflict in Sarajevo in 1992?

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: A social worker.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the armed conflict, were you required to perform some other work duties?

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: Yes. I was mobilised as a reserve policeman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In March of 1994, did you carry out any duties as a reserve policeman?

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there an incident which required you to attend a car park where there was -- where there had been some reports of a disturbance by children in 1994, in the month of March?

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: Why, yes. We received a complaint in the police station that some children were tampering with a car, damaging a car, and that is why we went out and to the parking lot on Ante Babica Street, between numbers 1 and 3. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you resolved the complaint, did you hear some shooting?

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: That's right. We heard two individual shots.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to determine the direction from which you heard the shots come?

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: Yes. From the direction of the Home for the Blind, which is in Nedzarici and was controlled by Serb forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do after you heard the sound of shots?

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: We thought that we were being targeted, and we tried to take some cover, that is, leave the parking lot, this exposed open area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "we were targeted," who were you with?

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: I was with a fellow policeman, because we were a patrol team.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What time of day was it when you heard the shots?

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: Between 2.00 and 3.00 in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the weather like at that time?

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: It was a nice spring day, not really cold.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You said that you tried to take some cover. After that, were you told something by some nearby children?

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: Yes. There were some children who were at a nearby balcony in that building which was facing Nedzarici. They started shouting that someone had been injured.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you then make some investigations in relation to the report that someone had been injured?

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: Well, my colleague and I, we started to run to the place that was indicated by the children, and there we found a man who was lying on the grass.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you notice any wound on the man?

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: He was in a state of shock, and at one moment he didn't even know that he had been injured. He was occasionally -- he was drifting in and out of consciousness, and I remember they were trying to lift his clothes off to see whether he was really injured, and then we saw a wound, a bullet wound, on the left-hand side of the abdomen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to obtain from the man any information, including his name?

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: Yes. Name, surname, and the address.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember those details at the moment?

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: Ivan Franjic, the Trg Solidarnosti number 11. I remember it because after the incident my colleague and I, we went to his family to let them know that he had been injured, that he was in one of the hospitals.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do in relation to him after you observed the injuries?

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: We stopped the first car that was passing by. We put him in the car and the car then went in the direction of the city.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that, did you receive some further information in relation to other injured person?

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: Yes. When the car left with this first injured person, the children and the people started shouting that another person had been injured, and we then ran a little further down, perhaps some 70 or 80 metres from that spot, and we found also an elderly person who was on their knees, holding onto the left-hand side of the abdomen, where we could see the blood. And again, we stopped one of the cars, one of the vehicles. We put him in the vehicle and he was taken to one of the hospitals. I don't know which one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us something further as to the nature of that injury to the left-hand side of the abdomen? In particular, were you able to see any internal parts of his body?

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: As for the first man, yes. When we lifted his shirt, his top that he was wearing, I remember that there was no blood. There was a wound around which we could see some part of some internal organs. I don't know which one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Were you able to take from the second man details as to his name and address?

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: No. I believe he lived in Ante Babica 5. Because it happened so quickly and because he was obviously in great danger and he was living in one of the nearby houses, and we couldn't take any personal details from him. We found that from the neighbours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember those details now?

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: I think Augustin Vucic, and I think the address was Ante Babica Street number 5.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What date was it that these events happened?

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: Early April. 10th of April, maybe, 15th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, -- I withdraw that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you make a statement to the criminal department on the 25th of February, 1995 in relation to these matters?

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I ask that the witness be shown a copy of that statement signed by him in order to refresh his memory as to the date. I have copies available for my learned colleague and Your Honours, together with translations into the English language. I propose to have the witness identify the statement and then refresh his memory as to the date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could it be done by just reading it, Mr. Ierace, so that we don't -- yes, please. Let me just have a look at it and we'll return it then later on to Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have before you a document that has down at the bottom some numbers, being 00268150?

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise your signature to the left and at the bottom of the page?

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that indeed a photocopy of the report to which you just referred?

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In that report, did you say: On 13 March -- do you see the words -- I withdraw that. Do you see at the beginning of the second paragraph, there's a reference to the date on which these events occurred?

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the date on which those events occurred, having regard to your report?

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: On the 13th of March, 1994.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Might that be returned, and I ask that the witness be shown a map, which is Exhibit P3115. Perhaps that could be placed on the ELMO. The second -- sorry. The left-hand half of the map in particular.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, did you make a statement to an investigator from the Office of the Prosecutor with the Tribunal on the 14th of November, 1995?

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time that you did that, did you place some marks on a map to indicate certain things?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, I think we have not yet received a copy of the map that's on the ELMO now. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this that map?

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I note, Mr. President, there was not an answer to the previous question, so I'll ask that again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you place some marks on the map to indicate certain things on the 14th of November, 1995?

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise your signature on the map which is to your right?

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you place the marks on the map which appear in blue ink?

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that map, in particular, there appears to the left a building which has a circle around it and an arrow going from it. What did you mean to indicate by the circle around the building and the arrow going from it?

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: This is the place where we found the wounded person and the place where the shots had come from.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Would you please take the pointer on the desk in front of you. It has a white tip on it. Would you please place the end of the pointer on the place where you say the shots had come from.

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think earlier you described that building as the School for the Blind; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, what did you mean to indicate by the little circle which appears on the road Ante Babic?

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: This is where we found the wounded person, the location where he was lying.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think you said you found two wounded persons. Which particular one was located at that point, or were both located at that point?

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: The first person was found where the little circle is, and the second person we found a little further down, about 70 to 80 metres, by that next intersection, the street crossing the Square of International Friendship, Trg Solidarnosti.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I think you said the first person's name was Ivan Franjic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, there appears to be a cross on the map as well. What does that indicate?

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: This is probably a place where we found the second person, the second wounded. Q.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, might that be returned, Mr. President. I withdraw that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the map as well, near the circle, there appears to be a line on Ante Babica. What does that represent?

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I'll rephrase it. Was there anything else that you remember indicating on the map apart from the School for the Blind and the position of the two men?

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: I marked from which side, in relation to the wounded, the barricade was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whereabouts does the barricade appear on the map? And perhaps you could point to it.

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: Here. This is where the barricades were.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I ask that the witness be shown photograph P3279Oa.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise what appears in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is that?

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: You can see the intersection where the barricade was, where the injured was, the first injured, the first wounded person. You cannot see where we found the second wounded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Do you see on that photograph the School for the Blind?

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: No, because in the meantime, as I can see, several buildings, or rather, some houses have been built.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please take your time and look at the photograph carefully. First of all, did the School for the Blind have one building or more than one building?

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: It consisted of several buildings, but they were of different height. How shall I put it?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see on the photograph in front of you any of the buildings for the School for the Blind?

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: Yes. Here, behind this red house. Here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please take a blue marker pen and circle the building or buildings which you recognised as belonging to the School for the Blind.

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, the circle has passed over a building which appears to be white, have some windows on the left-hand side, and a dark roof, and that's to the top left of the circle. Do you know whether or not that building is one of the School for the Blind buildings?

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: It's hard to find one's bearings because many buildings have been built in the meantime.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, you said that --

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: I think it could be this one. It could be that building. That could be the Institute for the Blind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For the benefit of the record, could you circle that building as well with a separate circle, the one you just pointed to.

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you place a 1 alongside the first circle and a 2 alongside the second circle.

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, I draw your attention firstly to the road which runs from the intersection in the foreground to the area of the School for the Blind. Do you know the name of that street?

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: This used to be called Branko Bujica Street, but now I believe it's called Srebrene Bosne Street, something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the place where that street meets up with Ante Babica Street, were there any barricades at the time that these two men were shot?

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: Yes, on this intersection here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps you could draw a line across that intersection in the approximate place of the barricades which existed at that time.

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you referred, I think, to another barricade; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you see on that photograph where the other barricade was?

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: It was higher than here, further up there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you mean further to the left of the line you've already drawn?

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: Even -- yes, that's right. Yes. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Further to the left as one looks at the photograph; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any other barricades on Ante Babica Street at the time of this incident, that is, in this part of Ante Babica Street which appears in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: I can't recall now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the middle of the photograph there appears a house about two storeys high with a red-tiled roof. Could you just point to that house but not mark it.

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please don't mark it. All right. Now, at the time of this incident, was that house there?

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: As far as I know, it was not. There was nothing there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time that you attended these two men, do you remember whether you met anyone else who may have been with them at the time that they were shot?

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Behind the --

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: Other people came running later, as we were putting them into the car.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I referred you earlier to the house in the middle of the photograph. Behind it there is a high-rise building of about ten storeys, with white balconies. Could you please point to that building.

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Please don't mark it. Was that building -- first of all, was that building there at the time these men were shot, and if so, in what condition was it?

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: Yes, it was there, but it had been completely demolished. There was no windows, there were no doors. There was nothing, just walls.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would that be a convenient time, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace. Mr. Dziho, we'll have a short break. We'll adjourn until a quarter past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just before the break I was asking you questions about the position of barricades. At the time that these two men were shot, were there any barricades on the eastern side of this part of Ante Babica Street?

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: You'll have to help me. Where is east on this map?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Perhaps the witness might be shown the map, which is Exhibit P3115. And again, could the left-hand side of the map be placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please assume that north is at the top of the map, south is at the bottom, east is on the right-hand side, and west is on the left. After you have looked at the map, could you please then look again at the photograph, P3279Oa. Applying the same compass points, the view is looking west, so that the further side of Ante Babica Street is the western side and the side which is in the immediate foreground of the photograph is the eastern side. To be clear that we understand each other, with the pointer, could you please point to the eastern side of Ante Babica Street.

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Were there any barricades at the time the two men were shot on the eastern side of Ante Babica Street, that you recall?

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What sort of clothing were the two injured men wearing?

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: Well, the regular, the common civilian clothes. One had a jacket, I think. I think they are called omot, the second injured. And the first one had a cotton jacket. I believe it was brown.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time that you heard the two shots, which way were you facing in relation to the direction from which the sound of the shots appeared to come?

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: We were facing Nedzarici, that is, the direction from which the shots came.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Approximately how far were you and your companion from the area of the footpath on Ante Babica Street, where you understand the two men were shot?

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: Thirty to fifty metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the armed conflict, were there from time to time ceasefires between the opposing forces?

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any ceasefire in force on this day?

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: Yes, as far as I know. I mean, because the population behaved in a more relaxed manner. They could move more freely and they could move more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you mean by that that during ceasefires one noticed a distinct change in the behaviour of people in public places in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us a little more about that, the noticeable differences when there was a ceasefire and when there was not a ceasefire, in relation to the civilians?

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: Well, people were more relaxed. They moved about with more freedom, if I may put it that way. But the experience of previous ceasefires, and also following this incident, when the ceasefire was on, our task was often especially in areas exposed to the sniper fire, we would be given a task to warn those people, because the ceasefire often meant nothing. It happened that they were injured during ceasefires or there would be some unexpected shell hitting the civilians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you attended the two injured men, did you notice any military equipment or soldiers in the vicinity?

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: No, I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I ask that the witness be shown the following exhibits: P2477, which includes the English translation .1 P2476, which includes the English translation .1, and P2664, which includes the English translation .1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, would you assist us. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I think the first of those documents is P2477.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, would you please look at the document you've just been handed. Does it have on the top right-hand corner the numbers and letter P2477, handwritten at the top right-hand corner?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Perhaps the usher could point to the relevant part of the page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please do it -- if you point at whatever thing, Mr. Usher, would you please do it on the ELMO so that we can follow what you're ... Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Perhaps that could be turned to the B/C/S version, which is P2477.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, do you -- I withdraw that. Do you have before you what appears to be a medical discharge for Ivan Franjic?

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I think you said that that was the name given to you by one of the injured men that you attended on the 13th of March, 1994; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you look halfway down that -- I withdraw that. Would you please now turn to the next document, which I think is P2476. Does that appear to be a report, that is, a police report, dated the same date as this incident, which shortly recounts what happened?

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the person who appears to have signed that report, Enes Avdic?

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please now turn to the third document, which appears to be a death certificate in relation to Augustin Vucic. Do you have that before you?

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that the name given to you by one of the two injured men was Augustin Vucic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you in fact hear later that he had died from his injuries?

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And does this document indicate that he died on the 1st of June, 1994, that is, two and a half months later?

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, that completes examination-in-chief of this witness. I draw to the Trial Chamber's attention that in relation to the English translation of the discharge summary for Ivan Franjic, there appears to be a mistranslation of the date of admission and date of release. It's apparent on the face of the document that it's a mistranslation. The English translation records the year as being 1993, but when one looks at the B/C/S original, one can see that in fact it was 1994. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace. I think there are perhaps some more -- for example, the date and place of birth also seems to give 193/?/I. As far as I can read I can see 1930, but I'm afraid there are some more. Because also part of what has been on the date of admission is not very precise. I also see 03 and then 94 instead of ... Okay. Yes. Thank you, Mr. Ierace. Ms. Pilipovic, is the Defence ready to cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dziho, you will now be examined by Ms. Pilipovic, who is counsel for the Defence. Cross-examined by Ms. Pilipovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Dziho.

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us if you gave any statements to OTP investigators between 1995 and this day?

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you confirm that this was on the 14th of November, 1995?

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: I know that it was late 1995. I don't know the exact date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us if on the 20th of September, 2001, you spoke to the OTP investigators?

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: I don't remember the date, but I did talk with them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dziho, may I ask you one thing: You have, I think, the text moving in front of you in English. Would you please wait until the text stops moving, because otherwise, since you are speaking the same language, the interpreters cannot follow you. Yes? Please. And it will happen that you forget about it. I'll remind you. Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Dziho, you told us that in 1992 you were living in Sarajevo. Can you tell us in what part of the city did you live?

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: Novi Grad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you be more precise and tell us which part of Novi Grad?

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: It is the C-Faza, that is, Alipasino Polje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You told us that when the conflict broke out in 1992, you were mobilised. Can you tell us who made the decision on the mobilisation and where did you report?

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: I have to make a correction. I wasn't mobilised in 1992. I was mobilised on the 20th of September, 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You tell us that you were mobilised on the 21st of September, 1991. Can you tell us which authority mobilised you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, we might have a problem. The witness said the 20th of September, and you're, I don't know for what reason, referring to the 21st of September. It might be that there's a translation problem, but ...

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, can you tell us, in September 1991, when was it that you were mobilised?

utterances.speaker: FUAD DZIHO
utterances.text: The 20th of September.
