utterances.text: And had one of your neighbours fashioned a pipe in order to divert this groundwater so it could be collected in buckets and jugs and various other containers?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA
utterances.text: That is how it was. He did that. He made it, and we asked him, "Well, can we use it if there is any?" And he said yes, we could, and that is what we did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this source of water was approximately 150 metres from your house; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Pita, when the war started, how many children did you and your wife have?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA
utterances.text: Only Anisa, and Anisa was born after 20 years of marriage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was Anisa's birth date?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA
utterances.text: Anisa was born on the 16th of June, 1989.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it be fair to characterise your relationship with Anisa as one that is particularly close?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA
utterances.text: Well, from the very day that she became conscious of herself, to this day, and I think she is closer -- she feels closer to me even, I think, than to her mother.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it common for Anisa to follow you during those times when you're not at work, follow you around the house?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA
utterances.text: Non-stop.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did there come a time during the war in Sarajevo that your daughter Anisa was the victim of a sniper?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA
utterances.text: Yes. We really were very mindful. We took care that nothing happened to her. And we kept warning her not to come out, to go down to the cellar, because we were afraid.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall the date that your daughter Anisa was the victim of a sniper?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA
utterances.text: Yes, of course I remember it. I remember it as long as I live. The 13th of December. It was Sunday, in 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe for the Trial Chamber what you did that day, starting with the time when you woke up in the morning.

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Well, it was a night like any other night. We went to bed early and we also got up early, because there was no electricity or anything. So that was that. And so we got up this morning, and she did at the same time as my wife and I did. And my wife and I talked, and she said that I should bring some water, because we had to do some laundry, and for the bathroom. And Anisa heard that and said, "I want to come with you." And that is how we agreed, and around 10.00 or half past 10.00 -- why the you exactly -- we went off to get water and had some pot of about 20 or 30 litres, and she had with her some small bucket, a pail or something, of two or three litres, so that she could help me. And so we set off. She was holding me by the hand and we reached that water, where we were to fill the vessel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the weather like that day, Mr. Pita?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA
utterances.text: That day was overcast. There was no snow, but it was sort of foggy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the two of you then proceed to fill up your water cannisters?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA
utterances.text: No. No, we did not. When we got there, the woman whose house it is there, I asked her -- there were some people. I don't know who they were. And she said, "Just wait a moment until this water -- until they get the water and then you take it." And as I stood -- she also has a daughter, Alma is her name, perhaps a couple of years older than Anisa. And she was staying there and Anisa asked her, "Alma, would you come with Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. me home so that we can play together?" And her mother said, "No problem. Why not?" But I didn't feel like taking her along. I wasn't really for it. But since they liked each other, I didn't really want to say that, and I said all right. But then Anisa said, "Well, let's go," and they left and I stayed behind to get this water. And as they were about halfway from this water to the house, one could hear shots. And to tell you the truth, I panicked and I started reckoning, well, this way from that house and along the road one cannot see anything, because it is in a hollow, but they will get there. But they had left and I stayed behind. So my turn came and I spent some 10 to 20 metres to fill this water. And as I walked back home, some 10 or 20 metres away, a neighbour was standing there and asked me, "Ekrem, where have you been?" And I said, "Well, I have gone to get some water." And from this place one could see my terrace and I could see that something was wrong. That something was wrong. And he said, "Do you know that Anisa has been wounded?" And I felt very bad at that moment. I sipped a little bit of that water, but then I somehow made it to the house and entered the house and Anisa was with her mother and brothers and those neighbours and they were all inside. And she saw that I was panicky and not all right. She said, "Not my head. Not my head, dad. I was hit in my leg, Pop." And other people were fussing about her, but nobody was doing anything specific. Then I picked her up and I saw that she had been hit in her right leg, somewhere above the knee. And then I -- well, and I reckoned then that perhaps it wasn't dangerous, but I was afraid that perhaps there could be some internal bleeding because I knew more or less that that would not be all right. And then my wife, as we were, we took her to the health centre in Stari Grad and they examined her and noted that she had been hit, but the bullet had gone through. And at the same time, they forwarded -- they sent us to the orthopaedic surgery and we went there straight away. We got there and they cleaned up the wound and she cried and wept and it was horrible. But they dressed the wound and we took her back home. And when I got back home, I found all my relatives there. They were all there in the house. And meanwhile, my brother told me that they had found the bullet which had hit her and that it had ended up in a slipper or something. One could see the place where the bullet had hit, where the bullet had struck. But she was given all the medicines and were told that for about three weeks I should take her to the clinic every three or four days, or even more frequently, if need be, for the check-ups, so that my wife and I had to get there. And I must say, it was more difficult for me to carry this child which was 3 years and 5 months. It was three or four kilometres. Of course, we had to carry her every time, because there was no transportation. And because there was all the time some gunfire and shelling and all that. And that was worse for me than to wait at this water source. So we did that for 20 days and after that she went when it was necessary. But now she walks. She has not suffered any long-term effects, except when the weather changes, then she complains that her leg hurts. And that's the story.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Pita, when your daughter Anisa and her friend Alma left you at the water source to go back to your house, did you say anything to them?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA
utterances.text: I told them to take care, and I told Alma, "You're older, so look out. Be careful."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall if anywhere along the route between the water source and your house there was an area where pedestrians would be exposed to sniper fire?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA
utterances.text: No, no. No, no, no. Not a single spot. The only place where it could have happened, it could have been that terrace that had, plus, minus, five or six metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This would be the terrace to your house; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA
utterances.text: It is. It is, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After returning from the hospital, did you discuss with your wife whether or not Anisa was injured before she got home or after she arrived at your home?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA
utterances.text: Well, she returned home, because it was with me that she had gone to this water. When she came home, as she was entering the front door, that is what my wife told me, and that's -- yes, that's how it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did your wife tell you anything about what Anisa was doing at the time that she was shot?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA
utterances.text: Yes. When the two of them got there, she was wearing some slippers or something. That is, there were no laces on the footwear, so that she took them off and they entered the house so that they could collect their toys and go downstairs in the cellar to play. But Anisa did have some proper shoes, that is, something that she had with laces. So mother told her to take them off, because they were dirty, and then to go back. And when it happened, Anisa did not start crying, so my wife said she did not realise anything. She didn't realise what happened. And Anisa said, "Oh, mother, it hurts me here," and that is when my wife looked at it and saw it and that is when everybody came.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And from what had happened, did your wife deduce that your daughter had been shot while removing her boots that she had been wearing when she went to get the water with you?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA
utterances.text: Well, yes. She even thought that it was finished. And she said, "Mommy, mommy, it's not my head." But the girl held onto her leg where she had been hit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Pita, you mentioned a few moments ago that when you arrived back home, there were some brothers present. Whose brothers were at your house when you arrived after collecting the water?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA
utterances.text: My brothers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where in relation to your house did your brothers live?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA
utterances.text: A house below mine. We are next-door neighbours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did any other members of your family live in the immediate vicinity of your house?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA
utterances.text: Well, no. My brothers and a sister, that is, two brothers and a sister lived in that house below, and I was with my family in this other house above.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Pita, from the time you left your house on the 13th of December, 1992 with your daughter to collect the water, until the time you returned to your house, approximately how much time had elapsed?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA
utterances.text: About 45 minutes, maybe an hour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you returned to your house, approximately how many people had gathered to assist your wife?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA
utterances.text: About, plus, minus, 15, 20. Because, you know, the street and the houses are close by, so that everybody knew it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were at the hospital, did one or more of your brothers find the bullet that had struck your daughter?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA
utterances.text: I've already said so. My elder brother, he told me when he came back, yes, he told me that he had found it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he tell you anything about the type of bullet that he found in your house?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA
utterances.text: He didn't. He said it was, I think, 7.6 millimetres and that was a sniper bullet. I really am not an expert. I'm not conversant with these kinds of things, so I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do either your brother or yourself still have possession of this bullet?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA
utterances.text: No, unfortunately. I simply didn't want to have it with me, so my eldest brother, he took it. But after a while, I had another problem in the family. My second daughter was born. Unfortunately, it was very hard, and she spent a long time in the hospital. And my wife, the delivery was very difficult. And we left the country on the 24th of March, because of this little one. And when we returned in 1998, then I asked him, "Do you have it anywhere?" And he said, "No. I've misplaced it. I've lost it."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis, would this be a suitable moment to interrupt.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: If I could ask one question and then we'll break until tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Pita, on the day that your daughter was shot, how old was she?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA
utterances.text: I know every second of her life. Anisa was 3 years, 5 months, and 27 days old.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: This would be a very convenient place to stop, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mundis. Mr. Pita, as I indicated to you before, we are not able to finish your examination today at 7.00 and we have to stop. Tomorrow, in the afternoon, we'll continue, at a quarter past 2.00, in this same courtroom. We'll adjourn until 2.15 tomorrow in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 19th day of February 2002, at 2.15 p.m. 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
